name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.225.0 — /spec:mocks became the wireframe command over the walkthrough service: three states (SEED, SCREENS, APPROVED), gray json-render screen files, and rounds, notes and confirmations through the plugin's own client; a project without the walkthrough block confirms stories in the terminal. The old reviewer package, its contract file, the mock-app templates and the spec-paths mock-contract key are removed; genesis reads its counts from the seed and the latest round. 7.224.0 — The prototype freeze captures at the window size it writes into contract.json: states.json's viewport is resolved once, passed to every capture, and refused when malformed; a capture that recorded another size fails the freeze. The build capture gate replays each baseline's own recorded size (a contract naming a size its baselines never used no longer needs a re-freeze) and notes the disagreement. proto-capture --diff refuses two captures taken at different sizes instead of reporting every element as changed. The build's capture step names what the session must restore: prototype.url, a development build, the frozen states' data, and the sign-in file. 7.223.0 — The prototype freeze signs in and derives its tier. A host may declare prototype.storageState, a saved Playwright sign-in that every capture loads — at the freeze and at the build's capture gate; a non-string, missing or unreadable file refuses by name before a browser launches, and a login redirect names the stale sign-in or says to declare one. /spec:doctor flags a committed storageState file. The generated spec's tier is no longer hardcoded standard: --mark tests-derived matches the File Plan against the host's pipeline rules § Risk Tiers paths, and any hit refuses until the user passes --tier standard|critical; the spec's Rationale records the basis and the mark prints the derived tier. The grounding contract gains the storageState key, so the contract hash changes and hosts owe a /spec:doctor re-stamp.
